title: Location
description: A place in the game world, and the join point between narrative data and the engine's scenes: gates, spawn points, and interactables.

zone.description: Project-defined grouping of locations for the zone map, e.g. zone_docks, zone_uptown.

scene.description: Opaque scene key for the engine to resolve (scene name, addressable, resource path). Parlance never resolves it.

spawns.description: Named spawn points. Each id is expected to have a corresponding marker in the engine's scene; Parlance does not verify that. Mark the arrival point used when nothing named a spawn (new game, dev entry, a cutscene arrival with no door) with "isDefault": true.

isDefault.description: This is the location's default arrival point, used when nothing names a specific spawn. At most one per location, and exempt from the unused-spawn check since no exit needs to point at it.

exits.description: Transitions to other locations. Each exit may carry a gate condition and a gate type.

gateType.description: Project-defined presentation kind for this gate, e.g. locked_door, toll_booth, guard_post. Free-form on purpose: the vocabulary is per-project, not a Parlance concept. The engine maps it to whatever art/prefab represents that kind of barrier; Parlance only checks that a gateType is paired with a gate condition.

denialDialogue.description: Dialogue that plays when the player fails the gate condition.

interactables.description: Objects and NPCs the player can interact with at this location.

dialogue.description: For object/environment: dialogue to play directly.

character.description: For npc: runtime resolves the character's dialogue ladder (resolveCharacterDialogue).

trigger.description: How the player reaches this. walk_up (default when absent): a thing in space the player approaches. on_enter: plays automatically on entering the location when its showIf passes (arrival scenes, turnbacks). Ambient barks are walk_up — they are embodied by an unnamed extra at a marker, not auto-played.
